races.name: Marjorie Thompsett Auntie Marj Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Byron Hill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with highest RPR (106) but 66 days off and faces early traffic problems with 4 others wanting his position
runners_data.comment: 1-18 hurdles; third to better-fancied stablemate Cosmic Soul at Sedgefield (2m4f) latest.
runners_data.spotlight: Sole hurdles win at Carlisle (2m1f, soft; from 8lb higher) in October 2024; consistent this year, without necessarily looking ready to win again; third to better-fancied stablemate Cosmic Soul at Sedgefield (2m4f, good) nine weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Rickety Gate
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in the danger zone early, pulled up penultimate start raises stamina doubts over 2m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Back below last winning mark (Carlisle, 2m4f) but pulled up at Ayr on penultimate start, and weakened into seventh at Cartmel (2m6f; beaten over 13l) 12 days ago; others more convincing at this stage.

runners_data.name: Fine Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfect for this pace shape, stepping up to 2m4f for first time but progressive for in-form yard
runners_data.spotlight: Steady progress since joining this trainer, resuming winning ways over 2m here (good; 7-2, with Malangen third) latest; raised 7lb since, and tackles 2m4f for the first time; noteworthy that Patrick Mullins travels over from Ireland to ride.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front runner will set genuine pace, 18 days since last run ideal and course winner here
runners_data.comment: Reeled in after blasting off in front at Perth on Wednesday but kept on gamely for second
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 2m here (good; from 13lb higher) in June 2024; seems to be gradually working back to form, a staying-on third to Fine Point here (2m, good; 100-30 favourite) latest; hopes of reversal over 2m4f on 7lb better terms.

runners_data.name: Ushuaia Dancer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly positioned for late surge, 67 days off but trainer has runners ready first time
runners_data.comment: Returned from two-year absence with pleasing second in March; remains well handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Only win came courtesy of the stewards' at Newcastle (2m6f, heavy) in January 2024; was returning from a lengthy absence when runner-up to a Skelton-runner at Newcastle (2m4f; 18-1) in March; realistic prospect of easing conditions would aid his cause.

runners_data.name: My My My Delilah
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner suits the pace but 12-race maiden with recent poor form including pull-up here
runners_data.comment: Fair form in bumpers but yet to match that in this sphere, pulled up at Hexham 15 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 12-race maiden; pulled up over 2m here (soft) on penultimate start, and weakened quickly at Kelso (2m, good; sixth, beaten 21l) subsequently; continues to ease in the weights, now 17lb lower than back in January.

runners_data.name: Cuillin Ridge
runners_data.note: Prominent style risks early trouble, 97 days off after leaving Henry Daly, headgear removed may help
runners_data.comment: Stuck to his task very well when second of nine at Wetherby (3m1f, soft) last time
runners_data.spotlight: Ridden out to score at Huntingdon (3m1f, novices' handicap; good to soft; from 6lb lower) in March; has since left Henry Daly for £12,500; headgear removed, and interesting to see what the market makes of his chance off a three-month break; merits respect.

runners_data.name: Road To Rosley
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 0-12 record and beaten 50 lengths last time makes him hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win (0-12) and beaten almost 50l in a Cartmel maiden (2m6f; 100-1) a fortnight ago; no reason to expect better for this return to handicapping; the first one to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Follow The Leader
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 496 days off rules racing, even with point form improvement needed
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three maiden hurdles (massive prices) in late 2024/early 2025; productive in points (form 212) this spring, chasing home Getupearly at Witton Castle (3m) last month; tough to know what to expect but isn't totally dismissed.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from top yard but beaten huge margins in recent starts over similar trips
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in an Irish point but it's been modest stuff under rules; readily opposed
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in a point; five-race rules maiden; beaten 50l, 54l, and 36l, in three hurdle starts (2m-2m4f maiden/novices'); significant improvement is needed to make an impression on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Malangen will take the field along at a genuine gallop from the front, with Byron Hill, Rickety Gate, Cuillin Ridge, Road To Rosley and C'Mon So all wanting prominent positions behind him creating significant early congestion. This bunching of 6 runners in the first quarter-mile will create stop-start fractions and inevitable traffic problems approaching the business end. The genuine pace from Malangen combined with the prominent squeeze sets up a strong finishing kick from 2 out. Hold-up horses with patient riders who can find daylight late will have a decisive tactical advantage over those trapped in the early scrum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent bunch gets into a traffic jam from 3 out as expected
scenarios.body: The early pace from Malangen sets it up perfectly for patient riders to sweep past tired leaders up the hill. Fine Point and Ushuaia Dancer get clear runs from the back to capitalize on superior finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Clear Out
scenarios.trigger: If Malangen and Byron Hill can escape the prominent traffic and open up a decisive lead
scenarios.body: The two classiest front-runners get first run on their rivals and battle it out up the hill with the field stretched behind. Their superior ratings tell as the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivors
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can avoid the early squeeze and get a smooth run through
scenarios.body: Road To Rosley or C'Mon So benefit from the pace collapse of the front two and tactical difficulties of hold-up horses. They inherit the lead at the right time with enough stamina to see it through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Malangen stops quickly and the prominent bunch comes back to the field in a bunch
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between whoever can quicken best from 2 out. Form and class become secondary to who gets the best late split and has most left in the tank.

watchPoints.text: Watch Malangen's jumping early - if he makes mistakes the whole pace dynamic collapses and creates chaos
Byron Hill and Rickety Gate will be fighting for the same prominent spot - whoever loses that battle faces traffic nightmares
Fine Point stepping up to 2m4f for first time - if stamina runs out late it opens the door for hold-up rivals
Follow The Leader returning after 496 days off - watch market move as any support suggests hidden improvement
Cuillin Ridge without headgear for first time - early position crucial as prominent style risks getting squeezed

races.name: Most Important 3-Year-Old Race Today Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.note: Front-running style perfectly suited to weak pace scenario with proven flat ability at this trip
runners_data.comment: Minor honours in handicaps for new stable on all three starts this season, 1m2f last two
runners_data.spotlight: Productive on the Flat (best RPR 82), with plenty to admire about the manner in which he applied himself going down to King Of Berkshire at Redcar (1m2f, good to firm) on penultimate start; trainer/jockey supplied the wide-margin winner of this (One Horse Town) last year; looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from in-form Dan Skelton yard but 59 days since last run may blunt sharpness
runners_data.spotlight: Made progress - at his own rate - on the Flat, seeming to handle the extra yardage when fifth of nine on handicap debut at Nottingham (1m2f, good; 14-1) in April; bit to find with Sudbury Hill on Flat figures, but it would be foolhardy to dismiss a Skelton-trained jumps newcomer.

runners_data.name: Mount Eden
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with fade warning but strong hurdling pedigree through half-brothers
runners_data.comment: Modest form in two runs on AW, hard to fancy after a lifeless Gowran run, cheekpieces now
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't offer much on the Flat for Donnacha O'Brien (0-4) prior to changing hands; his half-brothers Waver and Gold Seal were both successful over hurdles (2m); a first ever Hexham runner for the County Wexford handler Shay Slevin.

runners_data.name: Cracking Anna
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with fade concerns and disappointing recent flat form for Michael Bell
runners_data.comment: Nicely bred and disappointing should she not be more competitive off this low a mark
runners_data.spotlight: Flat form for Michael Bell isn't overly encouraging, beaten in excess of 8l in a 1m2f Class 6 at Yarmouth (good; 12-1) six weeks ago; dam won over hurdles though (2m5f) and she's in pretty safe hands with Greenall and Guerriero; receives the 7lb fillies' allowance.

runners_data.name: Jambearee
runners_data.note: Prominent style with first-time cheekpieces but poor flat form and fade warning
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in four of his five runs including at Beverley last month; 4lb out of weights
runners_data.spotlight: Lowly rated on the Flat (0-6); never better than midfield in added cheekpieces at Thirsk (1m4f, Class 5; beaten over 10l, 40-1) three weeks ago; trainers sole representative in this in 2024 was an early casualty; stablemate of Steel Fixer.

runners_data.name: Steel Fixer
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner getting Nathan Moscrop suggests stable confidence despite maiden status
runners_data.comment: Overraced and hit traffic latest but that was at least a step up on his turf efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Flat maiden (0-6) but marginally higher-rated than stablemate Jambearee, and the fact that Nathan Moscrop takes the ride suggests he's their principal hope; raced too freely and weakened on AW at Newcastle (1m2f) on Tuesday; wears first-time cheekpieces.

races.paceDynamic: Sudbury Hill will dictate from the front with only token pressure from prominent runner Jambearee, creating a sustainable rhythm in the early stages. The moderate pace will allow the hold-up quartet (Tiny Riot, Mount Eden, Cracking Anna, Steel Fixer) to stay in touch without being stretched. However, three of the four hold-up horses carry fade warnings, suggesting stamina concerns when the pace lifts approaching the final hurdle. This tactical setup strongly favours the early pace-setters who can establish position without pressure and kick clear when the closers hit their limitations.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Sudbury Hill gets an uncontested lead and maintains rhythm
scenarios.body: His proven flat ability translates smoothly over hurdles while the fade-prone hold-up horses fail to pick up when it matters. Paul O'Brien can dictate the tempo and kick clear approaching the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If Tiny Riot or Steel Fixer overcome their historical limitations
scenarios.body: Dan Skelton's proven ability with hurdling debutants sees Tiny Riot travel strongly and pick up late despite his hold-up style. The moderate early pace allows him to conserve energy for a telling finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Jambearee improves dramatically for cheekpieces and hurdles debut
scenarios.body: The added headgear sparks significant improvement as he sits handy behind Sudbury Hill before asserting in the straight. His prominent style avoids the traffic issues that could hinder the hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Eden's pedigree translates immediately to hurdling success
scenarios.body: The half-brother to hurdle winners finds his niche over obstacles despite disappointing flat form. Donnacha O'Brien's change of environment provides the spark needed for improvement.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sudbury Hill's jumping technique on debut as any hesitancy will hand initiative to closers
Monitor Tiny Riot's fitness after 59-day layoff from Dan Skelton's normally sharp stable
Observe Jambearee's response to first-time cheekpieces in early stages for immediate improvement signs
Check Mount Eden's position turning in as his fade warning suggests stamina limitations
Watch Steel Fixer's early position as Nathan Moscrop's booking indicates trainer confidence

races.name: Marrill Group Stamping Futures Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: The Clonmel Kid
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who benefits from only one natural pace rival, bad mistake cost him here last time from similar mark
runners_data.comment: Has made a decent start over fences, winning at Newcastle last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Won on second chase start at Newcastle (2m4f, good; from 4lb lower) in April; still bang there when a bad mistake at the last proved costly here (3m, good; 9-2) latest; risks are attached in this slightly more competitive contest.

runners_data.name: Conquer The Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with devastating last-start form over track, 13lb rise is harsh but Ryan Mania's 25% strike rate helps
runners_data.comment: Well supported when landing his second success over C&D on his stable debut ten days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 2-2 for Adam Nicol, winning easily over 2m here (good; Dream Jet 35l away in third) 18 days ago; the handicapper has taken another hit - 13lb higher - but it mightn't be enough to thwart the hat-trick bid; the only slight reservation being this 2m4f trip.

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Prominent type who was 35 lengths behind Conquer The Breeze here latest, hard to bridge that gap despite 5lb lower than last win
runners_data.comment: Usually needs a run under his belt to hit form after a break but has a decent record here.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual course winner (2m), who sits 5lb below his last winning mark; finished a remote third to Conquer The Breeze here latest, so it's difficult to work out how he goes about making up such a deficit, even acknowledging more favourable terms.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse suited by 2m4f trip, 7-length C&D winner 18 days ago with just 5lb penalty looks fair
runners_data.spotlight: Saw it out well to get off the mark over fences (C&D), beating Out On Her Own by 7l 18 days ago; a 5lb rise looks fair - competitive off similar marks over hurdles - so he'll be a live contender.

runners_data.name: Halpha Soleil
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 107 days off, winless over fences in 13 attempts raises red flags
runners_data.comment: 0-12 over fences; creditable third after wind op at Doncaster last time; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win over fences (0-13); third at Doncaster (3m, soft; on first start since wind surgery) in February, but well beaten at Sedgefield a fortnight later; absent since (107 days) and now 5lb lower in the handicap; others far safer.

runners_data.name: Similar Story
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose 2024 form figures (5UP036) offer little hope despite 12lb drop
runners_data.comment: 1-22; rallied from a tough position when modest third at Kelso (3m; good, 22-1) latest.
runners_data.spotlight: No win since October 2024; now rated 12lb lower, but her form figures this year (5UP036) offer little encouragement, with even her Kelso third (3m, good; 22-1) a laboured one; blinkers replace cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Blizzard
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with breathing issues, twice pulled up at Newcastle after bleeding from nose
runners_data.comment: Good second at Kelso last autumn but pulled up both runs since
runners_data.spotlight: 0-18 under rules; just failed at Kelso (3m, good; beaten a neck) last October, but has had issues since, twice pulling up at Newcastle (bled from the nose on both occasions), and beaten 83l at Perth (3m) over three weeks ago; best watched.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Valley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making chase debut proper, 55 days since last run and weak recent form
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner (May 2024); little impact over hurdles (0-4) and it was a similar story on chase debut at Ffos Las (2m4f, good to soft; 16-1) in April; now 3lb lower, with Jack Tudor taking over in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Out On Her Own
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who led too long on chase debut here, needs to settle better under Kavanagh
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden under rules (0-10), but she posted a series of consistent efforts over hurdles; tried to make all in an added hood over C&D (chase debut) latest, succumbing to the stronger finish of Passengerontheship; is 5lb better off with 7l too find; the task isn't impossible.

races.paceDynamic: The Clonmel Kid and Dream Jet will likely set a moderate pace from the front, with Halpha Soleil, Cosmic Blizzard and Similar Story tracking prominently. The hold-up horses Conquer The Breeze, Passengerontheship, Manhattan Valley and Out On Her Own will sit in behind, but this is not a deep field and the pace won't be frantic over 2m4f. Without a natural tearaway leader, the tempo will be measured early before quickening from 3 out. This sustainable pace setup strongly favours the hold-up horses who can come with late runs, as the early leaders will have plenty left to kick but the patient riders will have the final say.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady early allowing hold-up types to close strongly
scenarios.body: The measured tempo suits Conquer The Breeze and Passengerontheship perfectly, letting them unleash finishing kicks. Both have winning form fresh and can exploit the tactical advantage of racing behind the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Sustain
scenarios.trigger: If The Clonmel Kid and Dream Jet maintain their advantage to the line
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the prominent racers to control the tempo and kick clear when it matters. Their superior ratings tell late on when the pace lifts from 3 out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders fold badly and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Multiple horses hit the front in the final furlong creating a messy finish where anything can happen. The lightweights and fresh horses benefit from the scramble.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Conquer The Breeze Hacks
scenarios.trigger: If Conquer The Breeze reproduces his dominant last-start form
scenarios.body: His 35-length superiority over Dream Jet here 18 days ago suggests he's operating at a different level despite the 13lb rise. Ryan Mania simply needs to time his run and he wins pulling up.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Blizzard has twice pulled up with breathing problems and could exit early again
The Clonmel Kid made a bad mistake at the last fence here previously and jumping lapses could prove costly
Conquer The Breeze's 13lb penalty is severe but his 35-length superiority here suggests he's well ahead of these
Halpha Soleil returns after 107 days off and is still winless over fences from 13 attempts
Manhattan Valley is essentially a chase debutant after one poor run and could surprise at big odds

races.name: Hexham Racecourse Holiday Home & Caravan Park Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Always Busy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs the pace to collapse; 33 days off suggests freshness but may need the run after a fall last time
runners_data.comment: Sound effort when third to Wicked Thoughts last month; still unexposed over marathon trips
runners_data.spotlight: 1lb above last winning mark (3m, Southwell); knocking on the door at Taunton (3m4f; third) on penultimate start, and might have had a role to play in the Norfolk National at Fakenham (3m5f) latest but for falling three out.

runners_data.name: Giovanni Change
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent record on good ground; trainer's 1/12 strike rate is concerning but horse has proven 3m ability
runners_data.comment: Six course wins; respectable third over C&D since Wetherby success in March; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Admirable Market Rasen specialist (six wins there); won over 3m at Wetherby (good; from 2lb lower) in March, but hasn't been at his best since; uncharacteristically laboured (never travelling) when remote third latest; bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Lakefield Flyer
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace is strong; 5lb claimer reduces burden but recent Plumpton run was moderate over shorter trip
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins have come at Downpatrick (2m3f); plugged on to finish a modest second at Plumpton (2m1f, good; beaten 21l) 11 days ago; that should have given him confidence though - fell at Killarney prior - and this extra yardage could suit.

runners_data.name: Foxinthebox
runners_data.note: Prominent style from point-to-point background; 24 days since last run ideal but jumping under Rules remains question mark
runners_data.comment: Made all, turning over odds-on favourite, in three-runner point at Pusk (3m) 18 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Won back-to-back 3m points at Overton and Pusk, prior to finishing a creditable third in a hunter chase at Perth (3m; beaten 4l, 12-1) 24 days ago; with the suspension of hunter chases, he now switches back to a handicap for Susan Corbett.

runners_data.name: No Regrets
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with course winner's knowledge; immaculate jumping last time and trainer's perfect 2/2 record encouraging
runners_data.comment: Veteran who is suited by good ground; 2nd over C&D in October, but well beaten since
runners_data.spotlight: Stayed on to win this off topweight back in 2023, and gamely back in the winners' enclosure over C&D (from 5lb lower) latest; his jumping was immaculate that day, with his trainer stating that he had drawn benefit from being able to dominate; this rates as a tougher test.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent Perth win; 5lb claimer helps but quick turnaround from double-header may have left mark
runners_data.comment: He's run well in defeat over 3m here on his last two starts, most recently yesterday
runners_data.spotlight: Dug deep to resume winning ways at Perth (2m4f, good to soft; 15-8 favourite) over three weeks ago; that was his second run there in the space of 24 hours (third over 3m previous day); 4lb higher with blinkers applied, but Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim lessens that burden; key player.

runners_data.name: Lights Are Green
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying just 10st 3lb; returning to form after poor 2023 but needs to prove stamina over this extended trip
runners_data.comment: 2023 race winner off 5lb higher (good); struggled badly here and elsewhere last season.
runners_data.spotlight: Won off this mark (beat No Regrets by a neck) over C&D in May 2023; struggled last year, often pulling up, but gave an indication he's back in better shape when third to the in-form Halfway House Lad at Cartmel (3m1f, good; 20-1) a fortnight ago; worthy of inspection.

runners_data.name: West Lawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won here 18 days ago; 3lb claimer reduces weight but benefited from rival's error in breakthrough success
runners_data.comment: 0-19 over fences and has struggled in her last two starts, both over C&D.
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a final-fence error from The Clonmel Kid to get off the mark over fences at the 20th attempt over C&D (good; 10-1) 18 days ago; effectively 6lb higher from out of the weights today and her task is tougher; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Tell Me Again
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with pointing background; stable debut unseating suggests jumping concerns and lacks proven form over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a 3m point at Loughanmore for Tom Dreaper last October; badly hampered and unseated rider on stable debut, but left toiling behind Passengerontheship (beaten 78l) over 2m4f here 18 days ago; tough to consider on that evidence.

races.paceDynamic: No Regrets stands alone as the confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from the start, with Giovanni Change and Foxinthebox likely to track him in second and third. The lack of genuine pace pressure means No Regrets can control the tempo through the early stages, setting sustainable fractions that suit his stamina reserves. Over this 3m trip on good ground, the race will develop into a tactical affair where those able to travel kindly and produce their best effort from the 2f pole will prosper. This setup clearly favours prominent runners who can stay close to the pace without being drawn into early speed battles, giving them first strike when the real racing begins.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Holds Up
scenarios.trigger: If No Regrets maintains his galloping rhythm and the pace stays steady throughout
scenarios.body: The front runner's jumping accuracy and stamina prove decisive as he controls every call, with those tracking him unable to quicken sufficiently in the straight. This measured tempo allows the class horses to show their superiority without the race becoming a pure staying test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Behind
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses get the perfect opportunity to unleash their turn of foot, with the race becoming tactical rather than a stamina examination. Strong finishers benefit from the bunching effect and can pick off the pace-setters in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Giovanni Change or Foxinthebox apply pressure to No Regrets from the 3f pole
scenarios.body: The race develops into a battle between the pace angles, with those positioned handily getting first run on the leaders while the hold-up horses struggle to close the gap. Experience and tactical positioning prove crucial in a finish between the early leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If No Regrets falters or makes a crucial jumping error in the straight
scenarios.body: The race opens up dramatically for horses coming from off the pace, creating opportunities for improvers and those with questionable recent form. Chaos benefits the outsiders who can stay out of trouble and capitalize on the leaders' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: No Regrets at the fences - any jumping error will open the race up dramatically for those tracking behind
Giovanni Change's early positioning - if he gets too keen tracking the leader he may not have enough left for the finish
Always Busy's jumping rhythm - needs to be fluent to make up ground from his customary hold-up position
The pace through the middle section - if it becomes crawling it will turn into a sprint finish favoring hold-up horses
Sir Carnegie and West Lawn coming off recent wins - watch for signs of a quick turnaround taking its toll

races.name: ogledigital.co.uk Google Ads Tailed Off Too? Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent Hexham record (four wins here) returning to best trip after decent comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: Four Hexham wins (2m-2m4f) and is rated 15lb lower than when last successful at Kelso (2m, Class 2) in May 2024; returned from a 204-day absence with a decent effort, runner-up to Banderas, over 2m4f here latest; respected, even if some of the others have more potential.

runners_data.name: Mojito Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Non-runner - prominent runner who had shown career-best form recently after wind surgery
runners_data.comment: An eye-catcher last time on fourth start in Britain when beaten a neck at Ascot in March.
runners_data.spotlight: French winner for Francois Nicolle; underwent wind surgery after finishing fourth at Newbury in February, and posted a career best when a fast-closing second to King Al at Ascot (2m, good; 25-1) in March; 4lb higher, with Harry Cobden travelling for this sole ride.

runners_data.name: Pyramid Place
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse without a win for over a year but track record suggests capable from this mark
runners_data.spotlight: 9-39 hurdles, but no win since quickening clear in a four-runner Class 2 at Kempton (2m5f, good; from 19lb higher) in November 2024; pulled up over fences (bled from nose) on final start for Harriet Dickin nearly four months ago; best watched on stable debut (£6,000 purchase).

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form who needs to bounce back from disappointing Kelso effort
runners_data.spotlight: Won over fences here (2m, good; in first-time blinkers - two finished) last June; runner-up at Newcastle (2m4f) in April, but low key at Kelso subsequently; returns to hurdles for the first time since finishing tailed off over C&D last October; others more appealing.

runners_data.name: Freddy Robinson
runners_data.note: Prominent type off long absence but proven over trip and showed good flat form recently
runners_data.comment: Sole win on the Flat came here and he's been second over C&D on his last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Dug in to score on his last spin over hurdles at Market Rasen (2m, good to soft; from 3lb lower) in December; runner-up three times in succession on the Flat at Beverley recently, beaten 2l there (1m4f; 13-8 favourite) just ten days ago.

runners_data.name: Two Auld Pals
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who dominated over course and distance last time but faces 9lb rise for that success
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who returns from 12-week break on a good mark; no surprise if he features
runners_data.spotlight: Handled testing conditions best, bounding clear to make it 2-3 over C&D (soft; a 23l winner) four weeks ago; the handicapper has reacted, and he's now 9lb higher moving up into a Class 4; still enters calculations though, with 10lb claimer Gregor Walkingshaw retaining the ride.

runners_data.name: Stay In The Game
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner fresh from breakthrough hurdles win and likely to get uncontested lead
runners_data.comment: Beaten 18l when ninth of 20 in a Down Royal handicap three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Made the breakthrough over hurdles at the seventh attempt, getting the better of the long-odds-on favourite in a match at Huntingdon (2m, good to firm; 6-1) 12 days ago; what that form amounts to is questionable, and this Class 4 contest is much more competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Stay In The Game will lead unchallenged with limited pace pressure from just 7 runners. Mojito Des Mottes, Glory And Honour, and Freddy Robinson can sit prominent, but none are confirmed front-runners. The hold-up brigade of Well Educated, Pyramid Place, and Two Auld Pals will track from midfield/rear. This sustainable early pace followed by a sprint finish clearly favours the hold-up horses who can time their challenges late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Stay In The Game sets an uncontested lead allowing the closers to get into rhythm
scenarios.body: The genuine pace allows patient rides to be effective as Well Educated, Pyramid Place and Two Auld Pals can unleash finishing kicks. Stay In The Game's soft lead creates the perfect setup for closers to swoop late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Rank Advantage
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses Glory And Honour and Freddy Robinson press Stay In The Game earlier than expected
scenarios.body: This creates enough early pace to stretch the field and favour those handy to the pace. The hold-up horses get caught flat-footed by the increased tempo and can't make up the ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Stay In The Game gets such an easy lead that he can dictate completely and kick clear
scenarios.body: His recent Huntingdon win shows he can sustain a lead when allowed to bowl along. The closers struggle to peg back his advantage when he gets first run on the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the small field goes so slowly that it becomes a walking pace throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the last hurdle with little rhythm established. This neutralises the natural pace advantage and makes it a lottery based purely on who has most left in the tank.

watchPoints.text: Stay In The Game getting too easy a lead early - if he's 10+ lengths clear turning for home he could prove hard to peg back
Well Educated's jumping - any early mistakes from the 10-year-old could compromise his finishing kick from the rear
Two Auld Pals handling the significant weight rise after his dominant course and distance win last month
Freddy Robinson's fitness after 184 days off - needs to be sharp enough to track the early pace
Glory And Honour's headgear changes and whether the blinkers that helped his chase win here return

races.name: Tricia Hughes Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 177-day break with useful form from higher marks, but long absence is a concern despite solid course record.
runners_data.comment: Went close here last month and ran okay in higher grade here subsequently
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful at his peak, and his last win came from a mark 13lb higher than today's at Uttoxeter (3m, good) in July 2024; hampered and unseated rider when last seen at Newcastle six months ago; difficult to assess how much ability remains at the age of 13.

runners_data.name: Sunset Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form including second to subsequent winner Perseus Way, suits the likely pace scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Likely to be in the mix but probably remains vulnerable for the win off this sort of mark.
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up to Thursday's Hamilton scorer Perseus Way over 2m4f here (soft) on penultimate start, and bettered that on RPR's when third to Banderas subsequently; reliable but this step back up to 2m7f mightn't work in her favour; stable won this last year with Pinot Rouge.

runners_data.name: Jeteye
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in great form with 12-1 C&D win 18 days ago, but 4lb rise takes him back to problematic triple-figure mark.
runners_data.spotlight: Rediscovered a spark, scrambling home over C&D (good; 12-1) 18 days ago; a 4lb rise takes him back to a triple-figure mark (traditionally struggles from that position) but he isn't one to write off, with this track tending to bring out the best in him.

runners_data.name: Abbey Scope
runners_data.note: Prominent type moving up in trip after strong Kelso win 31 days ago, upward trajectory and trip extension both positive.
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner here in April 2025; pulled up over hurdles last time but could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Added to debut bumper win, hitting the line strongly to score at the third attempt in a handicap hurdle at Kelso (2m5f, good) 31 days ago; moves up in trip (ideal on pedigree) from a 6lb higher mark, with that form franked at Southwell by the third-placed Larkfield Lusive.

runners_data.name: Stylish Recruit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with useful course form but saddle slipped excuse last time masks true ability, needs to bounce back.
runners_data.comment: 2m4f win at Hexham last month; better than last run when his saddle slipped; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Game winner here (2m4f; from 2lb lower) in April; excuse next time (saddle slipped) but less competitive at Kelso (2m5f, good; fifth, beaten 10l) a fortnight ago; needs to bounce back against rivals with a fair amount of upside.

runners_data.name: Robert d'Ores
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three C&D wins but struggling for form in 2024, course experience his main asset.
runners_data.comment: All 3 wins have been over C&D, including this race in 2025; on last winning mark; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Three C&D wins, the most recent when keeping on well to repel Lelantos (from 2lb higher) last October; struggling for form in 2026 and has undergone further wind surgery since his last appearance five weeks ago; isn't the likeliest.

runners_data.name: Ebselysees
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with back-to-back Perth wins but 7lb rise since latest success makes task harder.
runners_data.comment: Something has clicked after back-to-back wins at Perth; feared after a 7lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Back in the groove since joining the doubly represented Susan Corbett, winning back-to-back at Perth (3m/3m2f); raised a further 7lb since latest win, but that is effectively offset by the returning Rebekah Duffy; worthy of serious consideration in hat-trick mission.

races.paceDynamic: Dinons will likely lead or share the early pace with fellow prominent runners Jeteye, Abbey Scope, and Ebselysees, creating a reasonable gallop over this staying trip. With multiple horses wanting to be handy, the pace should be honest but not breakneck, particularly given the 2m7½f distance that encourages patience. The absence of confirmed hold-up specialists beyond Sunset Hill and Robert d'Ores means the pace won't collapse. This setup favours horses with tactical speed who can position prominently and have something left for the finish, rather than pure hold-up horses who may find insufficient pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace Favours Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners (Dinons, Jeteye, Abbey Scope) set a solid tempo without going too fast early.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a true test where horses positioned handy can kick clear, while hold-up horses find insufficient pace collapse to close the gap. Prominent runners with stamina reserves and recent form shine.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Burns Out Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners (Dinons, Jeteye, Abbey Scope, Ebselysees) engage early and create a demanding gallop.
scenarios.body: The early pace setters tie up in the final half-mile, allowing Sunset Hill and Robert d'Ores to pick up the pieces from their patient hold-up positions. Late closers benefit from the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Dinons dictates a conservative tempo with other prominent runners content to sit behind.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last hurdle where natural speed and recent sharpness matter most. Horses like Jeteye and Stylish Recruit, who have shown recent spark, can quicken best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Suits Experience
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes messy with no clear leader as prominent runners hesitate early.
scenarios.body: The race fragments into a tactical affair where course experience and jumping accuracy become crucial factors. Robert d'Ores' three C&D wins and Stylish Recruit's course form could prove decisive.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Dinons shows any signs of rustiness early given his 177-day absence, as this could disrupt the expected pace scenario.
Monitor the pace closely in the early stages - if Jeteye, Abbey Scope and Ebselysees all go forward together, it could set up perfectly for the hold-up horses.
Keep an eye on Stylish Recruit's jumping and saddle security after the equipment failure last time out.
Watch Sunset Hill's position turning in - if he's in touch on this likely pace setup, his strong recent form suggests he'll be dangerous.
Observe Abbey Scope's stamina reserves over this longer trip as he steps up significantly in distance from his Kelso win.
